title: Javascript Objects
body:
[[Object Literal]]

The same idea as a C++ [[Object]] with the type declarations taken away. A JavaScript object
is a bag of key/value pairs, written directly rather than instantiated from a [[Class]]:

```js
const employee = { id: 34, name: "bob", role: "manager" };
employee.salary = 10000;    // fields can just appear
```

The differences that matter next to C++:

- **No type, no declaration.** There is no class to write, and no compiler to complain.
- **Fields are added and removed at run time**, which a [[Structure]] cannot do.
- `employee.name` and `employee["name"]` are the same thing, so field names are data.
- Methods are just fields holding functions.

Kept in this course's notes because it is the cleanest way to see what a class actually buys
you: the C++ version costs a declaration and gives you the compiler checking every field
access. Full treatment is [[Object Literal]] and [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]].
